title: Flaky tests and quality gates
summary: Find tests that lie, stop them blocking everyone, and decide what must be true before merging.

steps.title: Flaky tests
body: A **flaky** test passes and fails on the **same code**. Common causes:
- timing: `Thread.Sleep(100)` hoping a background task finished; real clocks (`DateTime.Now`) near midnight
- shared state: tests that depend on run order or on data another test left in the database
- the outside world: real network calls, random ports already in use, unseeded `Random`
Flakiness is corrosive: once people learn "just re-run it", they re-run real failures too.
```text
test              commit   result
Checkout_works    a1b2c3   ✔
Checkout_works    a1b2c3   ✘    ← same commit, different result: flaky

steps.prompt: `OrderExpires_after_30_minutes` fails about once a week, always shortly after midnight UTC. What is the most likely cause?
options: It reads the real clock and a date boundary changes the result; inject a clock (`TimeProvider`) instead
The CI runner is too slow
The test needs to be retried three times
steps.explain: Tests that read `DateTime.Now` behave differently at boundaries. .NET 8's `TimeProvider` lets tests use a fake, fixed clock.

steps.title: Handling a flaky test
body: ```text
detect ──► quarantine ──► fix root cause ──► un-quarantine
(same commit,   (still runs, but     (remove sleep,    (back to blocking)
both results)   does not block)      isolate data)
Automatic **retries** hide flakiness; if you use them, report "passed on retry" so the problem stays visible. Never quarantine forever:
give each quarantined test an owner and a ticket.

steps.prompt: Put the flaky-test response in order.
lines: Spot a test that both passed and failed on the same commit
Quarantine it so it no longer blocks merges
Open a ticket with an owner
Find and fix the root cause
Return it to the blocking suite
steps.explain: Quarantine buys time; the ticket makes sure the time is used.

steps.title: Quality gates
body: A **quality gate** is a rule the pipeline enforces before a change may merge or deploy. In GitHub this is **branch protection**:
required status checks must be green, plus required reviews.
Typical gate:
- all tests pass
- coverage ≥ the agreed floor (e.g. 80%) and does not drop much from `main`
- no high/critical vulnerabilities in dependencies
- at least one approving review
A gate must be **objective and fast**. If people regularly bypass it, it is measuring the wrong thing.

steps.prompt: Complete the step that fails the build when coverage is under 80% (Coverlet MSBuild properties).
steps.explain: Coverlet fails the test run when line coverage is below `Threshold` percent.

steps.prompt: Test history for one commit is below. Which tests are flaky? One per line, alphabetical.
steps.explain: `Search_paginates` fails consistently: that is a real bug, not flakiness.

steps.prompt: Select **all** practices that make a test suite less flaky.
options: Each test creates its own data with unique ids
Wait for a condition with a timeout instead of a fixed sleep
Inject the clock and random seed
Run tests in a fixed alphabetical order so state leaks are consistent
Retry every failed test five times silently
steps.explain: Forcing an order hides coupling instead of removing it, and silent retries hide flakiness.
